plan.title: Lab 7 proposed preflight tells learners to activate a proposed file, skipping promotion

narratives.Description: Lab 7 proposed preflight tells learners to activate a proposed file, skipping promotion
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

Module 7 teaches two separate lifecycle moves:

```text
task deft:scope:promote -- xbrief/proposed/<scope>.xbrief.json
task deft:scope:activate -- xbrief/pending/<scope>.xbrief.json
```

Lab 7 Task 1 then shows a live proposed preflight failure. On 0.119.5 the pinned engine exit is 1 and the Task wrapper is 201, as documented. The stderr I retained is:

```text
xBRIEF is in xbrief/proposed/ -- only xbrief/active/ (or legacy vbrief/active/) is eligible for implementation.
  Expected: `task xbrief:preflight -- xbrief/active/<story>.xbrief.json` (legacy: `task vbrief:preflight -- <path>`).
  Run `task scope:activate -- xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json` (or legacy `task vbrief:activate -- {path}`) before spawning an implementation agent.
```

The command that produced it used `--vbrief-path` against an xBRIEF file:

`xbrief:preflight --vbrief-path xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json`

Module 7 already notes that 0.119.5 help and Task descriptions retain some `vBRIEF` wording. It does not record that the live next-action line tells the learner to **activate a proposed file**, skipping promotion.

## Pain

I am being trained to treat command output as the next safe action. The first fail-closed diagnostic in Lab 7 names a recovery that contradicts the lesson I just read:

- course: promote proposed → pending, then activate pending → running
- live stderr: activate the proposed path

A mid-level engineer who follows the printed remediation would skip the promotion evidence Lab 7 exists to show. The lab helper continues through promote then activate, so the taught sequence works, but only if the learner ignores the engine’s own next command.

The `--vbrief-path` flag and `legacy vbrief/active/` text compound the Module 1/2 naming rule that new work uses xBRIEF 0.8.

## Proposed fix

In Lab 7 Task 1 / Module 7 expected-failures, quote this exact stderr and classify it:

- the eligibility fact is correct (proposed is not active)
- the printed `scope:activate` on a proposed path is retained 0.119.5 wording, not the consumer route
- the lab’s next move is still `deft:scope:promote` on the proposed file

Optionally ask the product to print promote-then-activate for proposed preflight. Until that changes, the course has to teach the disagreement at the first sighting, not only as a generic vBRIEF footnote.

## Re-verification

Live 0.119.5 `evaluate()` and `directive xbrief:preflight --vbrief-path xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json` both exit 1 with this message:

```text
xBRIEF is in xbrief/proposed/ -- only xbrief/active/ (or legacy vbrief/active/) is eligible for implementation.
  Expected: `task xbrief:preflight -- xbrief/active/<story>.xbrief.json` (legacy: `task vbrief:preflight -- <path>`).
  Run `task scope:activate -- xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json` (or legacy `task vbrief:activate -- {path}`) before spawning an implementation agent.
```

That matches the issue body. `formatActivateHint` substitutes the rejected path into `ACTIVATE_HINT`. The vbrief:activate parenthetical keeps a literal `{path}` because only the first placeholder is replaced.

`TRANSITIONS.activate.allowedSources` is `pending` only. `runTransition("activate", proposedPath)` returns `ok: false`: `Invalid transition: 'activate' requires file in pending/. File is in proposed/.` plus `formatUnreachableTransitionHint`: `deft scope:promote -- xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json` then `deft scope:activate -- xbrief/pending/2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json` (`auto-promote from proposed/ is refused`). `xbrief:activate` `SOURCE_FOLDERS` is the same pending-only set.

Pinned dest SHA:

- `labs/fixtures/07-scope-lifecycle/lifecycle-lab.mjs:327` runs `xbrief:preflight --vbrief-path` on the proposed delivery file, writes `proposed-preflight.json`, then `deft:scope:promote` on that proposed path and `deft:scope:activate` on the pending path.
- `curriculum/modules/07-scope-lifecycle.md:125-126` teach those consumer spellings. Lines 129-131 already record vBRIEF help/Task-description spelling as a documentation disagreement.
- Lab 7 Task 1 asks that both outputs name the proposed/active boundary and that evidence land before promotion.
- Lab 7, Module 7, and the Lab 7 solution expected-failures tables preserve the exit and continue through governed transitions. None classify the printed next command.
- SOURCE-NOTES Module 7 and SOURCE-BASELINE already record `--vbrief-path` as a legacy option name, vBRIEF help-card spelling, unprefixed `task` vs consumer `deft:` namespacing, and engine exit `1` / Task `201`. None record the activate-on-proposed next-action line.

## 1. Identity sentence “retained 0.119.5 wording” — `blocks-the-design`

Evidence: issue proposed-fix bullet 2 calls the printed `scope:activate` on a proposed path “retained 0.119.5 wording.” Module 7:129-131 and the SOURCE-NOTES Module 7 disagreement table already record vBRIEF help-card spelling, `--vbrief-path`, and unprefixed `task` forms. The live next-action line is `ACTIVATE_HINT` (`evaluate.js` default `buildReject` hint) substituting the rejected proposed path into a pending-only verb. Origin-freshness already special-cases that same hint once active+running have passed, because activate cannot apply there.

Failure mode: a bound recut is absorbed as another vBRIEF-spelling row. Task 1 still only checks the proposed/active eligibility clause. The unclassified next-command line stays in the retained JSON.

Disposition: the identity sentence that can bind is: 0.119.5 proposed-preflight stderr appends `ACTIVATE_HINT` with the rejected path, naming `scope:activate` on a proposed file. The eligibility clause in that same stderr is correct. The lab’s next move remains `deft:scope:promote` on the proposed file. Those two surviving bullets are the first-sighting classification.

## 2. Pain “skip the promotion evidence” — `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: issue Pain says a mid-level engineer who follows the printed remediation would skip the promotion evidence Lab 7 exists to show. The 0.119.5 activate path from proposed/ fails closed and then prints promote-then-activate. The helper already promotes after writing the JSON.

Failure mode: later measurement against activate-from-proposed makes the warrant look false, and the first-sighting recut is dropped with it. The remaining gap is silence: Task 1 and the recovery tables never classify the printed next command in `proposed-preflight.json`.

Disposition: recut Pain to that silence. The learner is trained to treat fail-closed output as the next safe action; the retained stderr names a command that cannot apply from proposed/; the lab still promotes. Quote the exact stderr at Task 1 and classify the next-command line there.

## 3. First-sighting vehicle — `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: Lab 7 Task 1 already inspects `proposed-preflight.json`. Expected-failures tables already classify the proposed-preflight exit. SOURCE-NOTES Module 7 already has a recorded-disagreement table. SOURCE-BASELINE already records the proposed-preflight command and the eligibility fact.

Failure mode: a new classification surface would duplicate those vehicles and miss the verifier that already walks Task 1, the helper, and SOURCE-NOTES (`scripts/verify-module-7.mjs`).

Disposition: put the first-sighting classification on the Task 1 confirm list, the expected-failures recovery cell, and one SOURCE-NOTES Module 7 disagreement row. Inventory stops there.

## 4. `--vbrief-path` compounding — `footnote`

Helper `:327` and SOURCE-BASELINE already record the legacy option name. It sits in the same command that prints the next-action line. It is a separate recorded disagreement. Folding it into this identity recut would again land on an existing SOURCE-NOTES row.

## 5. Optional product remainder — `footnote`

`buildReject` default-appends `formatActivateHint` on the folder-ineligible path. Origin-freshness already supplies a different hint. `formatUnreachableTransitionHint` already prints promote-then-activate when activate is requested from proposed/. The optional product remainder is that preflight folder-ineligible default. The two-step printer already exists on the activate surface.

## Injection / swarm lens

Applies: the recut splits authority inside one engine diagnostic. The eligibility clause is O7.1 evidence. The next-command line is an inapplicable redirect. A retained-wording identity would teach learners to discount the whole stderr, including the eligibility fact the outcome requires. The bindable split keeps the eligibility clause as the authorization fact and classifies only the next-command line as inapplicable from proposed/.

## Road-not-taken

Considered holding the curriculum recut until preflight itself prints promote-then-activate. Rejected: the helper already promotes; the course already records engine/course disagreements; activate-from-proposed already names the two-step. That remainder stays optional. Flip: if activate-from-proposed moved the file, or if Task 1 already classified the next-command line.

Steelman of “retained wording”: the stderr also carries vBRIEF and unprefixed `task` strings, and SOURCE-NOTES already knows how to record those. Smallest recut looks like one more wording row. Flip: `formatActivateHint` substituting the rejected proposed path into a pending-only verb, which is a different class than help-card spelling.
